release-notes.name: release-notes
release-notes.description: Shard a commit range across diff-reading summarizers, draft audience-aware notes, and fact-check them in both directions
release-notes.whenToUse: Cutting a release or backfilling a changelog, when the notes must be readable and provably cover the range. Input: {since, until?, audience?, out?, publication?}.

workflows.name: release-notes
workflows.description: Compute a Git manifest, summarize disjoint slices, fact-check with reviewRevise and write notes in code.

roster.name: Drafter
roster.description: Drafts and revises the notes from the summaries alone; uses no tools.

roster.name: FactChecker
roster.description: Checks the notes against the range in both directions; never edits.

roster.name: Summarizer
roster.description: Summarizes one disjoint slice of commits from its patch; never edits.

entries.name: Summarize
entries.description: Summarize one disjoint slice of the range from its patch.

entries.name: Draft
entries.description: Draft audience-aware notes from the slice summaries.

entries.name: FactCheck
entries.description: Fact-check the notes in both directions (the critic of reviewRevise).

entries.name: Revise
entries.description: Revise the notes from fact-check feedback (the actor of reviewRevise).

project-bootstrap.name: project-bootstrap
project-bootstrap.description: Detect the stack, approve one hashed setup plan, apply each concern in its own worktree, and prove the integration with code-run commands
project-bootstrap.whenToUse: Standing up a new project's tooling and CI from a spec, or retrofitting it onto a repository that lacks it; nothing is written before a human approves the plan. Input: {spec, stack?, concerns?}.

workflows.name: project-bootstrap
workflows.description: Approve one saved plan, isolate each setter, and verify its integration, settling command failures.

roster.name: Planner
roster.description: Plans disjoint setup concerns and argv verification commands; never edits.

roster.name: Setter
roster.description: Applies one approved concern to the files it owns, in an isolated checkout.

roster.name: Surveyor
roster.description: Inventories existing setup against the specification; never edits.

entries.name: Detect
entries.description: Choose or detect the stack and inventory existing tooling.

entries.name: Plan
entries.description: Plan disjoint concerns and the commands that prove them.

entries.name: Apply
entries.description: Apply one concern of the approved plan; the plan JSON comes last.

test-gap-filler.name: test-gap-filler
test-gap-filler.description: Find and rank the riskiest test gaps in one source file, write a test, and let code run the baseline and every mutation check
test-gap-filler.whenToUse: Hardening an operator-selected source file before a risky change or after an incident, when a test must be proven to kill mutants rather than claimed to. Input: {target, testFile, testCommand, behavior, maxGaps?, maxMutants?}.

workflows.name: test-gap-filler
workflows.description: Generate a test and mutation plan; code owns guarded writes, tests and interrupted-attempt recovery.

roster.name: GapFinder
roster.description: Finds test gaps in the target through one lens; never edits.

roster.name: Ranker
roster.description: Ranks the discovered gaps by blast radius; uses no tools.

roster.name: TestAuthor
roster.description: Proposes the test file and the mutants it must kill; never edits.

entries.name: FindGaps
entries.description: Find gaps through the coverage or the risk lens.

entries.name: Rank
entries.description: Rank the merged gaps by blast radius.

entries.name: PlanTests
entries.description: Propose the test file and independent single-anchor mutants.

incident-investigation.name: incident-investigation
incident-investigation.description: Hypothesis-free evidence collection over a pinned Git window, competing hypotheses, one falsifier each, and a confidence derived in code
incident-investigation.whenToUse: Post-incident root-cause analysis from a repository and symptoms, structured to resist first-plausible-story bias; read-only throughout. Input: {incident, since, until?, artifacts?, domains?}.

workflows.name: incident-investigation
workflows.description: Investigate an incident with a pinned Git window, read-only Codex roles and a structural confidence.

roster.name: Collector
roster.description: Collects facts for one evidence domain, without a hypothesis; never edits.

roster.name: Falsifier
roster.description: Tries to falsify exactly one hypothesis by checking its predictions.

roster.name: Reporter
roster.description: Writes the report from the verdicts and the confidence the workflow derived.

roster.name: Theorist
roster.description: Generates competing, falsifiable hypotheses from the pooled evidence.

entries.name: Collect
entries.description: Collect facts for one domain before any hypothesis exists.

entries.name: Hypothesize
entries.description: Generate three to five mechanically distinct, falsifiable hypotheses.

entries.name: Falsify
entries.description: Attack the predictions of exactly one hypothesis.

entries.name: Report
entries.description: Write the report around the confidence the workflow derived.

sdlc-orchestrator.name: sdlc-orchestrator
sdlc-orchestrator.description: Tailor a lifecycle, run each stage as a typed inline child under one run ID, and checkpoint every stage with a durable human review
sdlc-orchestrator.whenToUse: Driving a feature from requirements to a gated release with human checkpoints. Input: {goal, testCommand, allowedStages?, autoApprove?}; --workflow lifecycle-verification runs one gate alone.

workflows.name: sdlc-orchestrator
workflows.description: Tailor a lifecycle, run typed children inline and checkpoint stage-specific durable reviews.

roster.name: Intake
roster.description: Tailors the ordered stage plan to the goal and the repository; never edits.

roster.name: Reader
roster.description: Delegation ceiling for read-only child roles; never called directly.

roster.name: Writer
roster.description: Delegation ceiling for isolated child writers; never called directly.

workflows.name: lifecycle-document
workflows.description: Draft, gate and commit one lifecycle document.

roster.name: Author
roster.description: Drafts one lifecycle document from the goal and prior artifacts; never edits.

roster.name: Reviewer
roster.description: Gates one lifecycle document before the next stage builds on it.

workflows.name: lifecycle-implementation
workflows.description: Implement in an isolated checkout, verify in code, then integrate.

roster.name: Implementer
roster.description: Implements the goal in an isolated checkout; code runs verification.

workflows.name: lifecycle-verification
workflows.description: Run a QA or release gate command and settle its outcome as the stage gate.

Gatekeeper.description: Screens a stage whose gate passed when autoApprove is set.

entries.name: Intake
entries.description: Tailor the ordered stage plan.

entries.name: Draft
entries.description: Write one lifecycle document; the stage commits it.

entries.name: Review
entries.description: Gate one lifecycle document.

entries.name: Implement
entries.description: Implement the goal in an isolated checkout.

entries.name: Detect
entries.description: Choose or detect the stack and inventory existing tooling.

entries.name: Plan
entries.description: Plan disjoint concerns and the commands that prove them.

entries.name: Apply
entries.description: Apply one concern of the approved plan; the plan JSON comes last.

entries.name: Summarize
entries.description: Summarize one disjoint slice of the range from its patch.

entries.name: Draft
entries.description: Draft audience-aware notes from the slice summaries.

entries.name: FactCheck
entries.description: Fact-check the notes in both directions (the critic of reviewRevise).

entries.name: Revise
entries.description: Revise the notes from fact-check feedback (the actor of reviewRevise).

bug-hunt.name: bug-hunt
bug-hunt.description: Loop rotating-lens finder panels until two consecutive rounds find nothing new; settle a skeptic panel per candidate
bug-hunt.whenToUse: Exhaustive bug discovery on a codebase or subsystem, when you want the tail of the distribution and an honest count of what could not be decided. Input: {scope, maxRounds?, votes?, maxCalls?}.

workflows.name: bug-hunt
workflows.description: Run tolerant finder and skeptic panels, preserve uncertainty, and bound logical admissions.

roster.name: Finder
roster.description: Hunts concrete runtime bugs through one lens; never edits.

roster.name: Skeptic
roster.description: Tries to refute one bug claim by reading the code; never edits.

entries.name: Find
entries.description: Hunt one lens of one round; an empty list is valid.

entries.name: Refute
entries.description: One independent skeptic seat trying to refute a candidate.

acceptance-qa-batch.name: acceptance-qa-batch
acceptance-qa-batch.description: Per ticket: demonstrate every acceptance criterion with an approved probe that code runs in a prepared checkout pinned at one commit, then attack the feature with approved probes; pass = demonstrated AND unbroken, judged by exit codes
acceptance-qa-batch.whenToUse: Acceptance QA on finished work — verifying committed tickets meet their own criteria before merge or release, beyond unit-test green; report-only. Input: {tickets, probeCommand, prepare?, probeEnv?, scope?, maxTickets?, maxAttacks?, probeTimeoutMs?, prepareTimeoutMs?}.

workflows.name: acceptance-qa-batch
workflows.description: Demonstrate each ticket with approved probes that code runs, attack the ones that pass, and grade both by exit code.

roster.name: Breaker
roster.description: Writes attack probes against a demonstrated feature; code keeps what reproduces.

roster.name: Demonstrator
roster.description: Writes one probe per acceptance criterion against the pinned checkout; never edits.

roster.name: Ingester
roster.description: Copies tickets and criteria exactly and notes how probes can exercise the project.

entries.name: Ingest
entries.description: Copy the tickets and criteria verbatim and describe how probes can run.

entries.name: Demonstrate
entries.description: Write one probe per acceptance criterion, or say why it cannot be shown here.

entries.name: Break
entries.description: Write attack probes against a feature whose criteria were demonstrated.

acceptance-qa-deep.name: acceptance-qa-deep
acceptance-qa-deep.description: Decompose a ticket's acceptance criteria into binary checks, verify each against a pinned snapshot of the delivered work, and challenge every pass for letter-vs-spirit before code computes the verdict
acceptance-qa-deep.whenToUse: Gating whether finished work truly satisfies its ticket, the check "tests pass" does not make, including the criteria the developer forgot; read-only. Input: {criteria | criteriaFile, ticket?, base?, paths?, checkCommands?, maxCriteria?, maxPatchBytes?}.

workflows.name: acceptance-qa-deep
workflows.description: Pin the delivered work, check each decomposed criterion against it, challenge every pass and compute the gate verdict in code.

roster.name: Challenger
roster.description: Re-examines a passing criterion for letter-vs-spirit gaps; never edits.

roster.name: Checker
roster.description: Judges one criterion's sub-checks against the pinned snapshot; never edits.

roster.name: Decomposer
roster.description: Breaks the criteria into binary sub-checks and adds implied ones; uses no tools.

roster.name: Narrator
roster.description: Narrates the verdict the workflow computed for stakeholders; uses no tools.

entries.name: Decompose
entries.description: Break each criterion into binary sub-checks and surface the implied criteria.

entries.name: Check
entries.description: Answer each of one criterion's sub-checks from the snapshot and command output.

entries.name: Challenge
entries.description: Look for the narrow pass: letter satisfied, intent missed.

entries.name: Summarize
entries.description: One stakeholder paragraph around the verdict the workflow computed.

api-migration.name: api-migration
api-migration.description: Discover every call site of an old API, approve a disjoint file-group plan, migrate the groups in parallel isolated worktrees, then verify the integration once with code-run commands and repair the fallout
api-migration.whenToUse: Library swaps, API renames and contract changes with many call sites needing contextual judgment, the long tail codemods cannot handle; nothing is written before a human approves the plan. Input: {from, to, verifyCommands, notes?, paths?, searchTerms?, batchSize?, maxGroups?}.

workflows.name: api-migration
workflows.description: Approve a disjoint migration plan, migrate each group in its own worktree, and publish only a code-verified integration.

roster.name: Discoverer
roster.description: Finds every call site of the old API and groups them by file; never edits.

roster.name: Migrator
roster.description: Migrates one approved file group in an isolated checkout; code verifies it.

roster.name: Repairer
roster.description: Fixes one failure cluster within the approved files, in an isolated checkout.

roster.name: Triager
roster.description: Clusters code-run verification failures by root cause; uses no tools.

entries.name: Discover
entries.description: Find every call site and group the sites into disjoint file groups.

entries.name: Migrate
entries.description: Migrate one approved file group; the approved plan JSON comes last.

entries.name: Triage
entries.description: Cluster the code-run verification failures by root cause.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Fix one failure cluster within the approved files; the plan JSON comes last.

codebase-atlas.name: codebase-atlas
codebase-atlas.description: Survey a pinned commit into subsystems, deep-read each into a card in parallel, assemble an onboarding atlas in code, and run one completeness-critic repair round
codebase-atlas.whenToUse: Onboarding to an unfamiliar codebase, or generating the architecture doc a project never had; regenerating it needs replace. Input: {out?, maxSubsystems?, maxRepairs?, replace?}.

workflows.name: codebase-atlas
workflows.description: Survey a pinned commit into subsystems, deep-read them into cards, assemble the atlas in code and repair the gaps one critique finds.

roster.name: Critic
roster.description: Audits the assembled atlas against the repository for gaps; never edits.

roster.name: Reader
roster.description: Deep-reads one subsystem, or researches one repair, into a card; never edits.

roster.name: Surveyor
roster.description: Skims the layout and build files to partition the repository; never edits.

roster.name: Synthesizer
roster.description: Writes the overview and start-here list from the cards alone; uses no tools.

entries.name: Survey
entries.description: Partition the repository into subsystems from a code-built layout.

entries.name: Read
entries.description: Deep-read one subsystem into a card.

entries.name: Synthesize
entries.description: Write the overview and start-here list from every card at once.

entries.name: Critique
entries.description: Audit the assembled atlas for completeness against the repository.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Research one section's gaps into a corrected or new card.

dead-code-sweep.name: dead-code-sweep
dead-code-sweep.description: Find dead-code candidates through three search modalities, cross-check each with a default-to-keep skeptic, and remove an approved list in an isolated checkout that code verifies
dead-code-sweep.whenToUse: Codebase hygiene: removing provably unused exports and files without breaking dynamic or reflective consumers; report-only unless apply is set. Input: {scope?, apply?, verifyCommands?, maxCandidates?}.

workflows.name: dead-code-sweep
workflows.description: Sweep three modalities, keep every candidate a skeptic does not clear, and remove an approved list only after code verifies it.

roster.name: Remover
roster.description: Deletes the approved list in an isolated checkout; code runs verification.

roster.name: Skeptic
roster.description: Hunts a living reference for one candidate, keeping it when unsure; never edits.

roster.name: Sweeper
roster.description: Finds dead-code candidates through one search modality; never edits.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.description: Find candidates through one modality; each is blind to the others.

entries.name: Alive
entries.description: Try to prove one candidate alive, with a default-to-keep bias.

entries.name: Remove
entries.description: Delete exactly the approved list; the approved JSON comes last.

deep-code-review.name: deep-code-review
deep-code-review.description: Review a pinned change set across up to five dimensions, deduplicate in code, adversarially verify every finding, and synthesize a ranked report
deep-code-review.whenToUse: Pre-merge review of a branch, pull request or module change set when you want findings you can trust without re-reviewing them yourself; read-only, and committed changes only. Input: {base?, head?, paths?, dimensions?, maxChangedLines?, maxFindings?}.

workflows.name: deep-code-review
workflows.description: Review a pinned range per dimension, deduplicate in code, and report only findings a skeptic could not refute.

roster.name: Reporter
roster.description: Writes the markdown report from the verified findings alone; uses no tools.

roster.name: Reviewer
roster.description: Reviews the patch through one dimension in a snapshot of the head; never edits.

roster.name: Scoper
roster.description: Summarizes the pinned change and flags risky areas from its patch; uses no tools.

roster.name: Skeptic
roster.description: Tries to refute one finding at the head, refuting when unsure; never edits.

entries.name: Scope
entries.description: Summarize the pinned change and its risks without reviewing it.

entries.name: Review
entries.description: Review the patch through one dimension, in a snapshot of the head.

entries.name: Refute
entries.description: Try to refute one deduplicated finding, refuting when uncertain.

entries.name: Report
entries.description: Write the report from the confirmed findings and the review gaps.

dependency-upgrade.name: dependency-upgrade
dependency-upgrade.description: Upgrade a dependency: parallel changelog research and usage impact analysis, one approved plan applied in an isolated checkout, and a bounded code-run verify/triage/fix loop before publication
dependency-upgrade.whenToUse: Major-version dependency bumps where breaking changes are likely and usage is nontrivial; the operator names the install and verification commands, and nothing reaches the checkout before a human approves the plan and the commands pass. The commands run in the checkout that is published: what the install writes to the manifests is published, and an unignored file they write outside the plan refuses publication, so give verification commands ignored output paths. Input: {package, verifyCommands, toVersion?, maxFixRounds?, manifests?, installCommand?, maxUsageFiles?}.

workflows.name: dependency-upgrade
workflows.description: Research and map an upgrade in parallel, approve one plan, and publish it only after code-run verification and bounded repair rounds.

roster.name: Analyst
roster.description: Maps which files use which APIs of the package; never edits.

roster.name: Fixer
roster.description: Fixes one failure cluster in the files it owns, in an isolated checkout.

roster.name: Planner
roster.description: Joins the breaking changes with the usage map into a plan; uses no tools.

roster.name: Researcher
roster.description: Reads the changelog and migration guide on the web; sees no repository file.

roster.name: Triager
roster.description: Clusters code-run failures by root cause in the verified checkout; never edits.

roster.name: Upgrader
roster.description: Applies the approved plan in an isolated checkout; code installs and verifies.

entries.name: Research
entries.description: Read the changelog and migration guide for every breaking change up to the target.

entries.name: Impact
entries.description: Map which files use which APIs of the package, classifying every code-found file.

entries.name: Plan
entries.description: Join the breaking changes with the usage map into an ordered, scoped plan.

entries.name: Apply
entries.description: Apply the approved plan in an isolated checkout; the plan JSON comes last.

entries.name: Triage
entries.description: Cluster the code-run failures by root cause, for the fixers or, at the cap, for the report.

entries.name: Fix
entries.description: Fix one failure cluster forward, in the files it owns; the plan JSON comes last.

design-tournament.name: design-tournament
design-tournament.description: Four proposers with forced-diverse design philosophies, an independent anonymized judge panel scoring a fixed rubric that code tallies, and a synthesis that grafts or rejects each of the losers' best ideas
design-tournament.whenToUse: Architecture and product decisions with a wide option space, where a single-track designer would anchor on the first workable idea. Input: {brief, context?, judges?, crossHarness?, out?, publication?}. A parent under --require-grants maps Proposer, Judge and Synthesizer to a Claude ReadOnly ceiling and CodexJudge to a Codex ReadOnly ceiling, even with crossHarness off.

workflows.name: design-tournament
workflows.description: Propose under four forced philosophies, score anonymized proposals with an independent panel, tally in code and synthesize with recorded grafts.

roster.name: CodexJudge
roster.description: A judge seat on the other harness, so agreement spans two models; never edits.

roster.name: Judge
roster.description: Scores every anonymized proposal on the rubric as one seat; never edits.

roster.name: Proposer
roster.description: Designs for the brief in character, as one assigned philosophy; never edits.

roster.name: Synthesizer
roster.description: Builds the design on the winner and decides every losing idea; uses no tools.

entries.name: Propose
entries.description: Design for the brief in character, as one assigned philosophy.

entries.name: Judge
entries.description: Score every anonymized proposal on the fixed rubric as one independent seat.

entries.name: Synthesize
entries.description: Build the design on the winner and decide every losing idea by its ID.

docs-drift-audit.name: docs-drift-audit
docs-drift-audit.description: Decompose each prioritized doc at HEAD into quoted, checkable claims, verify each doc against the code, and report the drift or publish a human-approved patch for it, gated on verifyCommands when given
docs-drift-audit.whenToUse: Pre-release doc truthfulness check, or after refactors that likely invalidated READMEs and guides; report-only unless fix is set, and a fix run needs a clean checkout. Input: {paths? (Git pathspecs), fix?, maxDocs?, maxInventory?, maxClaims?, maxDocBytes?, evidenceCommands? (argv or {argv, okExitCodes}), verifyCommands?}.

workflows.name: docs-drift-audit
workflows.description: Rank the docs at HEAD, decompose each into quoted claims, verify them against the code, and publish a human-approved patch for the drift, gated on verifyCommands when given.

roster.name: Checker
roster.description: Verifies one doc's claims against the code at the base commit; never edits.

roster.name: Extractor
roster.description: Decomposes one doc, given in its prompt, into checkable quoted claims.

roster.name: Fixer
roster.description: Patches one drifted doc in an isolated checkout; code checks and publishes it.

roster.name: Librarian
roster.description: Classifies the listed docs by audience and priority from paths and headings.

entries.name: Classify
entries.description: Give each listed doc an audience and a priority from its path and headings.

entries.name: Extract
entries.description: Decompose one doc into atomic, checkable claims, each with a verbatim quote.

entries.name: Check
entries.description: Verify one doc's claims against the code, in order, with the evidence commands.

entries.name: Fix
entries.description: Patch one doc where its verified claims drifted, leaving true claims alone.

feature-factory.name: feature-factory
feature-factory.description: Conductor: run prd-decompose as a child, build an approved plan of disjoint modules in isolated worktrees, review each module with a deep-code-review child, repair confirmed findings, and publish only a verified integration
feature-factory.whenToUse: PRD-to-reviewed-code for a feature sized to one repository, from a clean checkout, or as the template for composing package workflows as typed children. Input: {prd, verifyCommands, codebase?, maxModules?, dimensions?, maxFindings?, maxCalls?}.

workflows.name: feature-factory
workflows.description: Decompose a PRD as a child, build an approved disjoint module plan in worktrees, review each module as a child, repair, verify and publish.

roster.name: Builder
roster.description: Implements one module inside its file areas, in an isolated checkout.

roster.name: Fixer
roster.description: Fixes one module’s confirmed review findings, in an isolated checkout.

roster.name: Planner
roster.description: Groups the backlog into disjoint, ordered modules; never edits.

roster.name: Reader
roster.description: Delegation ceiling for the children’s read-only roles; never called directly.

entries.name: Plan
entries.description: Group the backlog into disjoint modules that build in a fixed order.

entries.name: Build
entries.description: Implement one module of the approved plan; the plan JSON comes last.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Fix the confirmed review findings of one module, inside its areas.

entries.name: Lens
entries.description: Extract anchored work items through one lens; four other readers own the rest.

entries.name: Merge
entries.description: Merge the lenses into deduplicated, ordered tickets by judgment.

entries.name: Audit
entries.description: Walk the PRD backwards and report every coverage gap in the backlog.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Add or amend tickets for the gaps, quoting the PRD; code applies the patch.

entries.name: Scope
entries.description: Summarize the pinned change and its risks without reviewing it.

entries.name: Review
entries.description: Review the patch through one dimension, in a snapshot of the head.

entries.name: Refute
entries.description: Try to refute one deduplicated finding, refuting when uncertain.

entries.name: Report
entries.description: Write the report from the confirmed findings and the review gaps.

feedback-synthesis.name: feedback-synthesis
feedback-synthesis.description: Parse a feedback corpus into numbered items in code, fix a theme vocabulary on an even sample, tag disjoint shards in parallel, count, check quotes and rank by severity in code, and deep-dive the top themes into a quotable report
feedback-synthesis.whenToUse: Turning support, review, NPS or survey exports in the repository into ranked product themes with counts, severity and verbatim quotes; read-only, and every item is accounted for. Input: {sources, format?, textField?, fields?, focus?, deepDives?, severityWeight?, sampleSize?, shardSize?, maxShards?, diveItems?}.

workflows.name: feedback-synthesis
workflows.description: Parse a feedback corpus in code, calibrate a theme vocabulary, tag disjoint shards, count and rank in code, and deep-dive the top themes into a quotable report.

roster.name: Calibrator
roster.description: Fixes the theme vocabulary from a code-drawn sample; uses no tools.

roster.name: Diver
roster.description: Explains one theme's mechanism from its own items; uses no tools.

roster.name: Reporter
roster.description: Writes the summary and long-tail prose around code-rendered facts; no tools.

roster.name: Tagger
roster.description: Tags every item of one shard against the fixed vocabulary; uses no tools.

entries.name: Calibrate
entries.description: Fix the theme vocabulary from an evenly spread sample before any tagging.

entries.name: Tag
entries.description: Tag every item of one shard against the fixed vocabulary, with verbatim quotes.

entries.name: Dive
entries.description: Deep-dive one ranked theme from its own items: storyline, segments, one action.

entries.name: Report
entries.description: Write the summary, long-tail and emergent prose; code renders the rest.

flaky-test-hunt.name: flaky-test-hunt
flaky-test-hunt.description: Gather flaky-test suspects from git history, test-code smells and CI artifacts, stress-run each suspect in a tracked test file with the operator's single-test command for a measured flake rate, diagnose a mechanism for each confirmed flake, and publish approved fixes only after code re-stresses them
flaky-test-hunt.whenToUse: Unexplained CI red streaks, or auditing a test suite with a reputation for randomness; report-only unless fix is set. Input: {testCommand, scope?, testFiles?, passPattern?, runs?, maxSuspects?, fix?, fixRuns?, verifyCommands?, runTimeoutMs?, historyDepth?}.

workflows.name: flaky-test-hunt
workflows.description: Sweep three evidence sources, stress-run suspects in code, diagnose only measured flakes, and publish approved fixes only after code re-stresses them.

roster.name: Diagnostician
roster.description: Names the mechanism of one empirically flaky test and proposes a real fix.

roster.name: Fixer
roster.description: Applies the approved fixes in an isolated checkout; code re-stresses them.

roster.name: Sweeper
roster.description: Finds flaky-test suspects from one evidence source; never edits or runs tests.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.description: Find suspects from one evidence source; each sweeper is blind to the others.

entries.name: Diagnose
entries.description: Name the mechanism of one measured flake and propose a fix that removes it.

entries.name: Fix
entries.description: Apply exactly the approved fixes; the approved JSON comes last.

prd-decompose.name: prd-decompose
prd-decompose.description: Read a PRD through five parallel lenses, merge the items code can anchor into deduplicated, dependency-ordered tickets with acceptance criteria, and audit coverage backwards with bounded patch repairs
prd-decompose.whenToUse: Sprint planning from a PRD or spec, producing a backlog whose error states, migrations and instrumentation are ticketed, not just the happy path; composable as a typed child. Input: {prd, codebase?, out?, publication?, maxRepairs?, maxPrdBytes?, maxCodebaseFiles?}.

workflows.name: prd-decompose
workflows.description: Read a PRD through five settled lenses, merge anchored items into ordered tickets, and audit coverage backwards with patch repairs.

roster.name: Critic
roster.description: Walks the PRD backwards and reports the backlog coverage gaps; uses no tools.

roster.name: LensReader
roster.description: Extracts anchored work items from the PRD through one lens; uses no tools.

roster.name: Merger
roster.description: Merges the lenses into deduplicated tickets in dependency order; uses no tools.

roster.name: Repairer
roster.description: Adds or amends tickets for the coverage gaps as a patch; uses no tools.

entries.name: Lens
entries.description: Extract anchored work items through one lens; four other readers own the rest.

entries.name: Merge
entries.description: Merge the lenses into deduplicated, ordered tickets by judgment.

entries.name: Audit
entries.description: Walk the PRD backwards and report every coverage gap in the backlog.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Add or amend tickets for the gaps, quoting the PRD; code applies the patch.

prd-to-spec.name: prd-to-spec
prd-to-spec.description: Ground a PRD in the existing codebase, draft a technical spec through five lenses, optionally settle the top load-bearing decision with a design-tournament child, and audit the merged spec for implementability and PRD fidelity with one repair round
prd-to-spec.whenToUse: The step between PRD and tickets: producing a spec an engineer can build from without re-deriving the architecture inside the tickets. Input: {prd, codebase?, decideArchitecture?, judges?, crossHarness?, out?, publication?, maxPrdBytes?, maxCodebaseFiles?}. Under --require-grants nothing needs a grant: no role edits, and the tournament child maps onto the Reader and CodexReader ceilings.

workflows.name: prd-to-spec
workflows.description: Ground a PRD in the codebase, draft five technical lenses, optionally settle the top load-bearing decision with a design-tournament child, merge, audit twice and repair once.

roster.name: Auditor
roster.description: Audits the spec for implementability or PRD fidelity; uses no tools.

roster.name: CodexReader
roster.description: Delegation ceiling for the tournament child Codex judge; never called directly.

roster.name: Grounder
roster.description: Maps the architecture, conventions and constraints the spec must fit; never edits.

roster.name: LensWriter
roster.description: Drafts one technical lens of the spec and its contested decisions; never edits.

roster.name: Merger
roster.description: Merges the lenses into one spec and decides every contested item; uses no tools.

roster.name: Reader
roster.description: Delegation ceiling for the tournament child Claude roles; never called directly.

roster.name: Repairer
roster.description: Fixes the audited gaps in place, deferring to open questions; uses no tools.

entries.name: Ground
entries.description: Map the existing architecture the spec must fit; design nothing.

entries.name: Lens
entries.description: Draft one technical lens of the spec and record what it cannot settle.

entries.name: Merge
entries.description: Merge the lens drafts into one spec and decide every contested item by ID.

entries.name: Audit
entries.description: Audit the spec for implementability, or for fidelity to the PRD both ways.

entries.name: Repair
entries.description: Fix the audited gaps in place, deferring to open questions.

entries.name: Brief
entries.description: The design-tournament child's brief: the decision and its options.

entries.name: Context
entries.description: The design-tournament child's context: the grounding map and the PRD.

entries.name: Propose
entries.description: Design for the brief in character, as one assigned philosophy.

entries.name: Judge
entries.description: Score every anonymized proposal on the fixed rubric as one independent seat.

entries.name: Synthesize
entries.description: Build the design on the winner and decide every losing idea by its ID.

refactor-campaign.name: refactor-campaign
refactor-campaign.description: Find refactoring targets by measurable pressure, pin each target's behavior with a characterization net that code proves green, and refactor only behind every net after a human approves the plan
refactor-campaign.whenToUse: Behavior-preserving technical-debt paydown, where the safety net is the point, not an afterthought; report-only unless apply is set, and the checkout is untouched until then. Input: {testCommand (runs one test file appended as its last argument), scope?, goal?, maxTargets? (1 to 8), netRounds?, apply?, verifyCommands (at least one with apply)}.

workflows.name: refactor-campaign
workflows.description: Pin each ranked target with a code-verified characterization net, then refactor behind every net only after approval.

roster.name: NetWriter
roster.description: Adds characterization tests in an isolated checkout; code runs them.

roster.name: Ranker
roster.description: Ranks the surveyed targets by payoff against risk; uses no tools.

roster.name: Refactorer
roster.description: Applies one approved refactoring in an isolated checkout; code runs the nets.

roster.name: Reviewer
roster.description: Judges from the diff whether a refactoring is structural; uses no tools.

roster.name: Surveyor
roster.description: Finds refactoring targets by measurable pressure; never edits.

entries.name: Survey
entries.description: Find targets by measurable pressure, with evidence and current testability.

entries.name: Rank
entries.description: Select the best payoff-for-risk targets and name each refactoring.

entries.name: PinNet
entries.description: Write, or rewrite from its red output, one target characterization net.

entries.name: Refactor
entries.description: Apply one approved refactoring behind the nets; the approved goal and plan JSON come last.

entries.name: Review
entries.description: Judge from the diff and the net whether a refactoring is structural.

release-gate.name: release-gate
release-gate.description: Gate a release on six readiness dimensions with evidence: code runs the operator's tests and evidence commands, read-only assessors judge the pinned range, an independent Codex skeptic confirms each blocker, and the gatekeeper chooses only among the decisions a code-owned rule allows
release-gate.whenToUse: The go/no-go gate before shipping or promoting a release, decided from evidence rather than vibes. Run it on a checkout with no uncommitted or untracked files (ignored ones such as dependencies are fine) whose HEAD is the release; it gates since the previous tag by default, or since a given ancestor of HEAD. No agent edits the checkout, but the operator's commands run in it: one that moves HEAD or rewrites a tracked file refuses the gate, and an artifact that is not git-ignored refuses the next gate there; each pinned reader leaves a run-owned ref under refs/quiet-choir/ until workflow rm --refs. A go needs testCommands while tests is in blockOn: without them tests is cannot-check. Input: {since?, tagPattern?, policy?, blockOn?, testCommands?, evidenceCommands?, commandTimeoutMs?, maxRangeChars?}.

workflows.name: release-gate
workflows.description: Gate a checkout that is exactly HEAD on code-run tests and evidence, settled pinned readers, and a code-owned rule.

roster.name: Assessor
roster.description: Judges one readiness dimension from the range and command output; never edits.

roster.name: Confirmer
roster.description: Tries to downgrade one blocker against the code, on Codex; never edits.

roster.name: Gatekeeper
roster.description: Chooses among the decisions code allows and writes the rationale; uses no tools.

entries.name: Assess
entries.description: Judge one readiness dimension from the range and its command output.

entries.name: Confirm
entries.description: Try to downgrade one reported blocker against the code, the range and its output.

entries.name: Decide
entries.description: Choose among the decisions code allows and write a forwardable rationale.

requirements-to-prd.name: requirements-to-prd
requirements-to-prd.description: Extract quoted findings from raw requirement material through four lenses, draft a PRD traced to them, attack it with ambiguity, scope and feasibility critics, revise once, and surface unknowns as open questions
requirements-to-prd.whenToUse: Turning meeting notes, briefs, transcripts or feedback piles into a PRD honest enough to build from, with unknowns surfaced rather than invented; answers come back as input (a re-run redoes an earlier PRD at out through replace) or through durable question rounds. Input: {input, product?, answers?, questionRounds?, out?, replace?, publication?, maxMaterialBytes?}.

workflows.name: requirements-to-prd
workflows.description: Extract quoted findings through four lenses, draft a traced PRD, attack it with three critics, revise once, and surface unknowns as open questions.

roster.name: Critic
roster.description: Attacks the draft through one charter with quoted issues and fixes; uses no tools.

roster.name: Extractor
roster.description: Extracts quoted findings, unknowns and conflicts through one lens; uses no tools.

roster.name: Writer
roster.description: Drafts the structured PRD from the findings and revises it once; uses no tools.

entries.name: Extract
entries.description: Extract quoted findings through one lens; three other readers own the rest.

entries.name: Draft
entries.description: Draft the PRD sections from the findings, presenting conflicts as decisions.

entries.name: Attack
entries.description: Attack the draft through one charter with quoted issues and concrete fixes.

entries.name: Revise
entries.description: Apply the fixes; a fix that needs the product owner becomes an open question.

research-synthesis.name: research-synthesis
research-synthesis.description: Multi-modal lead sweep, ranked deep reads into claim and support pairs, a synthesis whose citations code checks, and one critic-driven round of targeted hunts
research-synthesis.whenToUse: Technology decisions, state-of-the-art surveys and due-diligence questions that deserve cited evidence over a single search pass. Read-only: web roles have only WebSearch and WebFetch, and local roles only file tools on a snapshot of HEAD. A context enables the local sweep in a Git repository with a commit; elsewhere it only grounds the prompts and the unsearched local territory degrades the result. The context reaches every role, web ones included, so it must hold nothing that may not leave the machine. Input: {question, context?, depth?}.

workflows.name: research-synthesis
workflows.description: Sweep for leads, deep-read the ranked top, synthesize with checked citations, and run one critic-driven hunt round.

roster.name: Critic
roster.description: Finds the answer's gaps and writes a targeted hunt for each; uses no tools.

roster.name: Hunter
roster.description: Runs one targeted web hunt for a critic gap; no file tools.

roster.name: LocalHunter
roster.description: Runs one targeted hunt in the pinned repository snapshot; no web tools.

roster.name: LocalReader
roster.description: Deep-reads one repository file at the pinned commit; no web tools, never edits.

roster.name: LocalScout
roster.description: Finds leads in a snapshot of this repository; no web tools, never edits.

roster.name: Reader
roster.description: Deep-reads one remote lead into claim and support pairs; no file tools.

roster.name: Scout
roster.description: Finds leads through one web modality; reads nothing in depth, no file tools.

roster.name: Synthesizer
roster.description: Writes the cited answer from the keyed readings alone; uses no tools.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.description: Find leads, not answers, through one modality whose charter names its blind spot.

entries.name: Read
entries.description: Deep-read one ranked lead, remote or local, into claim and support pairs.

entries.name: Synthesize
entries.description: Write the cited answer from keyed sources; a revision also addresses the gaps.

entries.name: Critique
entries.description: Find gaps with targeted hunt instructions, given the facts code checked.

entries.name: Hunt
entries.description: Run one targeted hunt for one critic gap, on the web or in the repository.

roadmap-plan.name: roadmap-plan
roadmap-plan.description: Decompose a spec into capabilities with a dependency graph that code checks, sequence them under three competing strategies, pick one by scored panel, stress-test it against the code-computed critical path, and render the revised roadmap in code
roadmap-plan.whenToUse: The milestone-altitude plan between spec and tickets: sequenced, gated, shippable phases with risks located, before prd-decompose or feature work per milestone. Input: {spec, horizon?, priorities?, out?, maxCapabilities?, maxSpecBytes?}.

workflows.name: roadmap-plan
workflows.description: Decompose a spec into a checked capability graph, sequence it under three strategies, pick and stress-test the winner, and render the revised roadmap in code.

roster.name: Critic
roster.description: Stress-tests the winning plan for the ways roadmaps fail.

roster.name: Decomposer
roster.description: Decomposes the spec into sized, rated capabilities and their dependency graph.

roster.name: Finalizer
roster.description: Revises the winning plan with the graft and resolves every stress-test problem.

roster.name: Judge
roster.description: Scores the competing plans against the priorities and picks the winner.

roster.name: Strategist
roster.description: Sequences the capabilities into gated milestones under one strategy.

entries.name: Decompose
entries.description: Decompose the spec into capabilities with a size, risk, value and hard dependencies.

entries.name: Sequence
entries.description: Group the capabilities into milestones under one sequencing philosophy.

entries.name: Pick
entries.description: Score the competing plans against the priorities, pick one and name a graft.

entries.name: Stress
entries.description: Hunt the ways the winning plan fails; the spec comes last.

entries.name: Finalize
entries.description: Revise the winning plan with the graft and resolve every stress-test problem.

security-audit.name: security-audit
security-audit.description: Map the attack surface of a pinned revision, sweep it with up to six specialist lenses, refute each located finding with a severity-scaled skeptic panel, and write a remediation report
security-audit.whenToUse: Defensive security audit of code you own or are authorized to audit: before launch, after inheriting code, or as a periodic sweep of sensitive surfaces. Read-only and committed code only; also set --max-run-cost-usd. Input: {scope?, lenses?, revision?, maxFindingsPerLens?, crossHarness?}.

workflows.name: security-audit
workflows.description: Map a pinned revision, sweep it per lens, refute each located finding with a severity-sized panel, and report the survivors.

roster.name: Auditor
roster.description: Sweeps the snapshot through one security lens for attackable flaws; never edits.

roster.name: CodexSkeptic
roster.description: A panel seat on the other harness, so a severe claim faces two models; never edits.

roster.name: Mapper
roster.description: Maps entry points, trust boundaries, secrets and dependencies; never edits.

roster.name: Reporter
roster.description: Writes the remediation report from the confirmed findings alone; uses no tools.

roster.name: Skeptic
roster.description: Tries to refute one finding as one panel seat; never edits.

entries.name: Recon
entries.description: Map the attack surface of the snapshot for the lenses that follow; no audit.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.description: Audit the snapshot through one lens, armed with the recon map.

entries.name: Refute
entries.description: One independent panel seat trying to refute a located finding.

entries.name: Report
entries.description: Write the remediation report from the confirmed findings and the gaps.
